# std/checksum

CRC-32 (IEEE, the one gzip, PNG and zip use) and Adler-32 (zlib). The CRC is computed
bitwise with no lookup table: constant work per byte, which suits worst-case-time
analysis and small bare-metal targets. Values are returned as i64 held to 32 bits.

```milo
from "std/checksum" import { Checksum }
```

## Example

```milo
print(Checksum.crc32("hello"))     // 907060870
print(Checksum.adler32("hello"))   // 103547413
```
